## Install R

Download R 4.4 or later from [CRAN](https://cloud.r-project.org) and run the installer for your platform (Windows, macOS, Linux). This project was built against R 4.5.3. Any recent 4.x release will work.

## Install Positron

Download [Positron](https://positron.posit.co) and install it.

Both Positron and RStudio are built by Posit, but only Positron keeps getting new features. RStudio keeps stability, security and bug-fix updates. Positron is built on the same open-source foundation as VS Code and runs R and Python side by side in one place. For anyone here who already works in Python day to day, the same editor covers both languages.

Once Positron is installed, open it and check it has found your R installation: bottom status bar -> interpreter picker, or `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P` -> "R: Select Interpreter".

If you already use RStudio, you can keep using it for this course. Everything works the same, apart from the Positron-specific shortcuts below.

## Positron keyboard shortcuts

A handful of shortcuts cover most of what you'll do in Positron day to day.

| Action | Mac | Windows |
|---|---|---|
| Open the Command Palette | `Cmd+Shift+P` | `Ctrl+Shift+P` |
| Toggle the file explorer (left panel) | `Cmd+B` | `Ctrl+B` |
| Toggle the Plots/Variables panel (right panel) | `Cmd+Option+B` | `Ctrl+Alt+B` |
| Insert a new code cell | `Cmd+Shift+I` | `Ctrl+Shift+I` |
| Run the current cell and move to the next | `Shift+Enter` | `Shift+Enter` |
| Run the current line | `Cmd+Enter` | `Ctrl+Enter` |
| Toggle the terminal panel | `` Cmd+` `` | `` Ctrl+` `` |

The Command Palette is where to find commands with no dedicated shortcut worth memorizing, like "Quarto: Run All Cells" or "Quarto: Run Cells Above": open it, then type the command name.

## Get the course materials

Go to the [course repository](https://github.com/franckalbinet/tidy-mirs) on GitHub, click **Code** -> **Download ZIP**, then unzip it. Open the unzipped folder in your editor, as described in [Open the project folder](#open-the-project-folder).

If you already use git day to day, cloning works just as well:

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
git clone https://github.com/franckalbinet/tidy-mirs.git
```

## Install the R packages

This project uses [renv](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/) to pin exact package versions, the same idea as Python's venv or conda. It gives you a project-local library instead of your regular R install. `renv.lock` records exactly what's installed. Everyone in the course runs the same versions we tested against.

### Open the project folder

Open the course folder itself, not a single file inside it:

- **Positron**: `File` -> `Open Folder…`, then choose the course folder.
- **RStudio**: double-click `tidy-mirs.Rproj` in the course folder, or use `File` -> `Open Project…` and choose it.

renv starts only when R starts inside the project folder, because the `.Rprofile` file in that folder activates it. The ZIP download includes this file, even though your file browser may hide it.

### Let renv install itself

You do not need to install renv yourself. The first time R starts in the project folder, renv downloads and installs itself. When it is ready, the console shows a line like this:

```{.default filename="Console"}
- Project '~/tidy-mirs' loaded. [renv 1.x.x]
```

renv may also say that some packages recorded in the lockfile are not installed. This is expected at this point. The next steps install them.

If you do not see the "Project loaded" line, check that you opened the folder and not a single file. Then restart R: in Positron, use the restart button in the Console panel; in RStudio, use `Session` -> `Restart R`.

This project was built with R 4.5.3. If your R version is different, renv shows a warning about it. You can ignore this warning: any recent 4.x release works.

### Install the build tools

renv installs the exact package versions in `renv.lock`. When a version is no longer the current one on CRAN, CRAN has no ready-made binary for it, and renv compiles it from source. For this, your computer needs a compiler:

- **Windows**: install [Rtools](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/), choosing the version that matches your R version.
- **macOS**: install the Xcode Command Line Tools by running `xcode-select --install` in the Terminal. If a later build fails with an error that mentions `gfortran`, install it from the [CRAN macOS tools page](https://mac.r-project.org/tools/).
- **Linux**: install your distribution's R development package, for example `r-base-dev` on Debian and Ubuntu.

If you already have these tools, go to the next step.

### Restore the packages

In the R console, run:

```{.r filename="Console"}
renv::restore()
```

renv lists the packages it is going to install and asks `Do you want to proceed? [Y/n]`. Type `Y` and press Enter.

The first run downloads and installs everything listed in `renv.lock` into a project-local library. It can take a few minutes, longer if some packages compile from source. It touches nothing outside this project folder.

### If renv fails

`renv::restore()` can fail behind a restrictive network proxy, on a locked-down institutional laptop, or in similar cases. If it does, install the same packages directly into your regular R library instead:

```{.r filename="Console"}
install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("mixOmics")

install.packages(c(
  "tidyverse", "tidymodels", "here", "opusreader2",
  "skimr", "plsmod", "prospectr", "resemble", "hexbin", "glue",
  "rules", "Cubist"
))
```

Run the two parts in this order. `mixOmics` comes from Bioconductor, not CRAN, so `install.packages()` cannot find it. `plsmod` needs `mixOmics`, and cannot install until `mixOmics` is there.

This gets you everything you need for the course. It isn't version-pinned. Let us know if something behaves differently from the demo.

## Check everything works


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(here)
library(opusreader2)
library(prospectr)
library(resemble)
library(plsmod)
library(rules)
library(Cubist)

packageVersion("mixOmics")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] '6.34.0'
```


:::
:::


If you installed the packages with `renv::restore()`, also check that your project library matches `renv.lock`:

```{.r filename="Console"}
renv::status()
```

It should report that no issues were found and the project is in a consistent state.

If that runs without errors, you're set up for the course.

## renv cheatsheet

Run these in the R console, with the course project open.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `renv::restore()` | Installs the package versions recorded in `renv.lock`. |
| `renv::status()` | Shows where your project library and `renv.lock` disagree. |
| `renv::install("pkg")` | Installs a package into the project library. Use `"bioc::pkg"` for Bioconductor packages. |
| `renv::snapshot()` | Records the packages you now have in `renv.lock`. |
| `renv::update()` | Updates the project's packages to their latest versions. |
| `renv::deactivate()` | Turns renv off for this project, so R uses your regular library again. `renv::activate()` turns it back on. |

You only need `restore()` and `status()` for this course. If you run `snapshot()` or `update()`, your `renv.lock` no longer matches the versions we tested against.
